answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a small deposit and build a public work history, so a sybil attacker cannot simply wander in with a fresh face each time. Honest agents accumulate trust like sediment settling in a lagoon, while a burned identity loses its deposit and must start over from zero. The umber stain of a past fraud stays attached to the record, so creating many throwaway identities costs far more than any single scam can earn.
